title: Optimize Guardrails — Threshold tuning scratchpad (Applied ML)
content:
Scratchpad / working notes. Not a spec.

Context
- We need default threshold values for Optimize apply gating across optimization types (quantization/batching/caching/routing tweaks).
- Goal: catch “real” user-visible regressions without blocking safe cost wins.
- This doc is focused on: candidate thresholds, metric distribution sanity checks, and FP/FN analysis using historical experiments and a few known incidents (quant-induced format drift, reasoning degradation, etc.).

Terminology (for myself)
- Baseline = current config on a route/model (the pre-apply state)
- Candidate = proposed Optimize config delta
- Suite = collection of prompt sets + graders producing metrics
- We will have both: (a) non-stat guardrails (hard constraints) and (b) statistical regression thresholds.

Assumptions (need to confirm in ADR / runner integration)
- Eval-harness “gating mode” outputs:
  - per-metric aggregate values + uncertainty (CI) where applicable
  - prompt-set revision + model version + config delta hash
  - run metadata: sample sizes, grader version, seed
- For thresholding we can rely on either:
  - delta-based rules (candidate - baseline)
  - or candidate must exceed absolute floor (for “must not go below” metrics)
- We likely need BOTH depending on metric.

Metrics in scope (current shortlist)
1) Task success / rubric
- task_success_rate (binary success judged by rubric or deterministic checker)
- rubric_overall (0–5 or 0–10 normalized to 0–1)
- helpfulness / correctness sub-scores (maybe later; keep v1 minimal)

2) Structured output / tool calling
- json_valid_rate (strict JSON parse success)
- schema_valid_rate (passes JSON schema)
- tool_call_valid_rate (function name + args parse)
- tool_call_accuracy (if we have ground truth tool + args; otherwise only validity)

3) Safety / toxicity
- toxicity_rate (binary; want non-increase or strict ceiling)

4) Factuality proxy (careful: noisy)
- citation_presence_rate / retrieval_consistency (only for RAG suites)
- hallucination_proxy_rate (LLM-judge; likely too unstable for hard gating in v1)

5) “Behavioral invariants” / formatting
- response_length_p50/p95 deltas (as proxy; can over-block)
- refusal_rate (if we have a refusal policy suite)


Historical data we used for tuning (rough)
A) Quantization A/Bs (internal) — last ~3 months
- ~68 experiments across 7 model families (Llama-ish, Mixtral-ish, Qwen-ish, etc.)
- Typical delta patterns:
  - small average change in rubric_overall (±0.01–0.03) but heavy tails for specific prompt types (math/logic, constrained JSON)
  - structured output regressions are “spiky”: json_valid_rate can drop 2–20 pts on a handful of prompts when it breaks

B) Batching/caching tweaks (runtime/config)
- ~41 experiments, mostly stable on rubric metrics
- main failure mode: output ordering/streaming chunking interacts with parsers; manifests as json_valid_rate drop / tool_call_valid_rate drop

C) Routing tweaks (fallback model variants)
- ~19 experiments
- tends to cause consistent rubric delta (model behavior difference) rather than spiky validity issues

D) Known customer-ish incidents (notes from support / internal)
- Quant profile transition caused formatting drift -> downstream JSON parser failures -> user-visible break
- Another case: quant improved latency but reasoning got worse on “long chain-of-thought” style prompts (rubric success down ~5–8 pts)


Distribution notes (quick sanity)
1) json_valid_rate distributions
- Many prompt sets are “near-deterministic”: baseline json_valid_rate often ~0.98–1.00.
- Candidate distributions:
  - Most changes keep within ±0.005.
  - Failure cases are distinct: 0.85–0.95 depending on severity; rarely subtle.
- Conclusion: thresholds can be relatively strict here without FP explosion, IF sample size is sufficient and prompts actually cover strict JSON.

2) rubric_overall (normalized 0–1) distributions
- Baseline variance depends heavily on grader noise.
- For LLM-judge rubric graders we saw std dev across re-runs about 0.01–0.02 on the same system/prompt set.
- For deterministic checkers (e.g., exact match / unit test) variance is ~0.
- Conclusion: for LLM-judge rubric, avoid “hair-trigger” deltas; prefer CI-based gating or min delta thresholds above noise floor.

3) task_success_rate
- As a binomial metric it behaves nicely if n is decent.
- But many suites today have n ~30–80, which yields wide intervals.
- Conclusion: we should encode minimum n per metric before we treat a regression as real; else fall back to “inconclusive” (timeout/insufficient sample) rather than pass.

4) toxicity_rate
- Typically low base rates (<0.5% on our internal corpora). Very sensitive to prompt set composition.
- Conclusion: we should use a ceiling rule (candidate toxicity_rate <= threshold) AND a non-increase rule vs baseline with small epsilon, but only if we have enough “sensitive” prompts.


Candidate threshold framework (proposal)
We should classify metrics into 3 threshold types:
A) Non-increase / delta-based (quality should not regress):
- rubric_overall, task_success_rate, tool_call_accuracy
B) Must-stay-high / floor metrics (format invariants):
- json_valid_rate, schema_valid_rate, tool_call_valid_rate
C) Must-stay-low / ceiling metrics (safety):
- toxicity_rate

Stat rule options (v1 candidates)
Option 1: Fixed delta thresholds
- Simple: fail if delta < -X (or candidate below floor)
- Pros: understandable, fast
- Cons: ignores variance, can cause FPs when n small or graders noisy

Option 2: CI-based thresholds
- Fail if lower bound of (candidate - baseline) CI < -X
- For floors: fail if lower bound of candidate metric CI < floor
- Pros: aligns with uncertainty
- Cons: implementation complexity + needs stable variance estimation

Current leaning: Use CI-based for rubric metrics where we have LLM-judge noise; use fixed thresholds for validity metrics.


Proposed defaults (for pilot) — NOTE: subject to change
All deltas are candidate - baseline.

Global minimums / data sufficiency
- min_prompts_total_per_suite: 60 (hard) for rubric-based gating
- min_prompts_total_per_suite: 40 (hard) for validity-based gating (because effect sizes are large)
- If below min: return INCONCLUSIVE (block apply in hard-block stage; allow override).
- Rerun policy: if inconclusive and user requests rerun, allow 1 rerun within 24h (to avoid flake loops).

1) Structured output (JSON / schema) — apply to any optimization touching runtime execution (quant/batch/cache) and to “structured output routes”
- json_valid_rate:
  - Floor: 0.98 (i.e., at most 2% invalid)
  - Delta: must be >= -0.005 (don’t allow more than 0.5% regression), BUT floor dominates if baseline was already <0.98.
  - Notes: floor of 0.98 seems strict; check against real customer data (some apps tolerate lower). Might need per-route overrides.
- schema_valid_rate:
  - Floor: 0.97
  - Delta: >= -0.01
- tool_call_valid_rate:
  - Floor: 0.98
  - Delta: >= -0.005

2) Tool calling accuracy (only where ground truth exists)
- tool_call_accuracy:
  - Delta: >= -0.01 (1 pt)
  - CI rule: lower bound delta >= -0.015 (if using CI)

3) General chat / instruction following
- rubric_overall (normalized to 0–1):
  - Delta: >= -0.015 (1.5 pts on 0–1 scale)
  - If CI available: lower bound delta >= -0.02
  - Rationale: noise floor ~0.01–0.02; we want to catch real regressions (quant reasoning drops were ~0.03–0.06)
- task_success_rate:
  - Delta: >= -0.02 (2 pts)
  - CI: lower bound delta >= -0.03

4) Safety
- toxicity_rate:
  - Ceiling: 0.01 (1%) for general suites
  - Non-increase: delta <= +0.002 (0.2%) if n sufficient and suite is “toxicity-sensitive”
  - Open: do we gate on toxicity at all for Optimize config changes? Product leaning yes for enterprise; unclear for self-serve.


Optimization-type-specific tightening/loosening
Quantization profile transitions
- Known failure modes: format drift, “subtle logic” regressions, longer tail of bad outputs.
- Proposal: require BOTH general chat suite + structured output suite if route supports structured output/tool calling.
- Threshold adjustments:
  - rubric_overall delta threshold tighten to -0.01 (from -0.015) for “reasoning-heavy” tagged workloads (math/logic/analysis)
  - json_valid_rate floor stays 0.98; delta stays -0.005

Batching/caching config changes
- Usually safe; failures show up in formatting/tool validity.
- Proposal: rubric suite optional unless change crosses a “risk boundary” (e.g., enabling speculative decode? increasing max batch tokens? changing cache eviction policy?)
- For v1: always run structured output suite for structured routes; run lightweight rubric suite (n=60) only on high-traffic routes.

Routing tweaks (switching fallback model)
- Main risk: consistent quality change rather than invariants.
- Proposal: rely on rubric + task_success; structured output only if route uses it.
- Threshold: rubric_overall delta >= -0.02 seems acceptable if cost win is large? (But product wants “no regressions”). Tentatively keep -0.015.


FP/FN analysis (rough, based on backtests)
Dataset used: 52 historical quant experiments where we have comparable suites; 33 batch/cache; 16 routing.
Labeling: “true regression” = flagged by at least 2 of (human spot check, deterministic failures, downstream bug reports, or very large metric shift).

A) json_valid_rate floor 0.98 + delta -0.005
- True regressions caught: 9/9 (all known format-break cases)
- FNs: 0 observed (but risk: suite coverage gaps)
- FPs: 2/52 (both were n=25–30; failure disappeared when n>80)
- Action: enforce min_n for validity metrics to reduce FPs; otherwise this rule is good.

B) rubric_overall delta -0.015 (CI lower bound -0.02)
- True regressions caught: 7/8
  - Missed one case: regression was isolated to a very specific prompt subtype underrepresented in suite (tool-augmented planning). Not a threshold issue, a coverage issue.
- FPs: 6/52
  - 4/6 were borderline deltas around -0.012 to -0.018 that didn’t reproduce on rerun.
  - 2/6 were grader drift (grader model updated between baseline and candidate run — need pinning!)
- Action:
  - Require grader version pinning + seed where possible
  - Prefer CI-based with rerun-on-borderline
  - Consider “gray zone” => manual review instead of hard fail?

C) task_success_rate delta -0.02
- True regressions caught: 5/6
- FPs: 3/41 (mostly small n)
- Action: minimum n + CI lower bound delta

Summary
- Most avoidable FPs are explained by:
  1) too-small n
  2) grader drift / non-pinned grader versions
  3) suite not covering the real failure mode (coverage gap)
- Most avoidable FNs are coverage gaps, not threshold values.


“Gray zone” idea (needs product buy-in)
Instead of binary pass/fail on borderline:
- Pass: meets thresholds with margin
- Fail: violates thresholds materially
- Review: within epsilon band (e.g., rubric delta in [-0.02, -0.015])
  - Behavior in control plane could be: soft-block (override required) for pilot
This reduces false hard-fails while still preventing silent regressions.

Suggested epsilon bands (pilot)
- rubric_overall delta:
  - Fail if < -0.02
  - Review if in [-0.02, -0.015)
  - Pass if >= -0.015
- task_success_rate delta:
  - Fail if < -0.03
  - Review if in [-0.03, -0.02)
  - Pass if >= -0.02
- json_valid_rate:
  - No gray zone (fail fast). Either it’s safe or it breaks.


Per-model-family notes (very rough)
- Mixtral-ish models: quant tends to hit tool_call_valid_rate more than rubric.
- Llama-ish: quant hits reasoning (rubric/task_success) more.
- Qwen-ish: seems robust on rubric, but we saw occasional schema_valid issues on very constrained outputs.
=> We likely need per-model-family threshold overrides or mandatory suite mapping (already tracked in quant guardrails policy work).


TODOs / open questions
1) CI calculation / implementation
- Are we doing bootstrap on prompt-level deltas? Or treating metrics as independent binomials/normals?
- For rubric_overall: likely bootstrap on per-prompt score differences.
- Need to ensure determinism in aggregation ordering (we already saw non-deterministic ordering causing flake).

2) Baseline strategy
- Baseline should be from same runner + same prompt-set rev + same grader version.
- If baseline is missing, do we:
  - run baseline first (adds time)
  - or use last known baseline cached for that exact config?
- My view: for high-risk changes (quant) run paired baseline+candidate; for low-risk allow cached baseline if recent (<7 days) and same versions.

3) Metric normalization
- If rubric is 0–5 in some suites and 0–10 in others: must normalize to 0–1 in harness output (or in policy engine). Prefer harness output normalized.

4) Sample size targets per workload
- Structured output suites need enough strict cases. If suite composition is weak, floor thresholds will “pass” even though real user prompts break.
- Need to coordinate with prompt-set coverage plan.

5) Customer-tier policy
- Do we allow “observe-only” for some tiers? (Product question)
- For enterprise, expect hard-block with override + justification.

6) Cost vs quality trade
- Some customers might accept small quality loss for large cost win; do we support per-tenant tuning in v1? If yes, need safe bounds.


Notes from last sync (2025-01-10)
- Jonas: wants CI-based by default for rubric, strict floors for structured output.
- Selene: agrees, but warns that grader stability is the bigger issue than thresholds.
- Logan: telemetry cardinality concerns if we log per-prompt; keep aggregates + artifact links.
- Olivia: harness can emit per-prompt details in artifact, but gating decision should rely on aggregate.

Appendix: quick table of candidate defaults (pilot)
Metric | Type | Default rule | min_n
- json_valid_rate | floor+delta | candidate >= 0.98 AND delta >= -0.005 | 40
- schema_valid_rate | floor+delta | candidate >= 0.97 AND delta >= -0.01 | 40
- tool_call_valid_rate | floor+delta | candidate >= 0.98 AND delta >= -0.005 | 40
- rubric_overall_norm | delta/CI | delta >= -0.015 (review band [-0.02,-0.015)) | 60
- task_success_rate | delta/CI | delta >= -0.02 (review band [-0.03,-0.02)) | 60
- toxicity_rate | ceiling | candidate <= 0.01 AND delta <= +0.002 (if sensitive suite) | 200? (tbd)

(End)
